articles.title: WordPress SEO plugin Rank Math compromised to backdoor websites
articles.summary: The Rank Math PRO WordPress plugin, downloaded from the official vendor website, was compromised and contained malware that installed hidden backdoors on affected websites. This supply-chain attack compromised the plugin distribution itself, putting thousands of website owners at risk without their knowledge. Attackers gained unauthorized access to websites through these backdoors, potentially enabling further malicious activities.
articles.whyItMatters: This attack demonstrates how trusted software distribution channels can be weaponized to compromise large numbers of websites simultaneously, making it critical for site owners to verify plugin integrity and monitor for unauthorized access. articles.title: Hackers hijack AOMEI update servers to secretly spread malware
articles.summary: Attackers gained unauthorized access to AOMEI's update servers and used a promotional feature in the company's backup software to distribute malware to users. The hackers temporarily modified configuration files to deliver the malicious payload before restoring them to cover their tracks, making the attack harder to detect.
articles.whyItMatters: This attack demonstrates a dangerous supply-chain compromise where legitimate software update mechanisms are weaponized to distribute malware at scale to end users who trust the vendor. articles.title: Bullhorn takes staffing platform offline to contain cyberattack
articles.summary: Bullhorn, a staffing software company, has taken its platform offline to stop an ongoing cyberattack from spreading further. The incident caused a complete system outage, preventing users from accessing the service. By disconnecting their systems, Bullhorn is attempting to isolate and contain the threat before it causes more damage.
articles.whyItMatters: This incident demonstrates how cyberattacks can completely disable critical business services, affecting thousands of staffing clients and job placements. It highlights the importance of rapid incident response and the real-world consequences when companies must go offline to protect data and systems. articles.title: OpenCode hack exposes API keys amid AI distillation attacks
articles.summary: OpenCode, an open-source AI coding project, suffered a security breach that exposed API keys belonging to some of its users. These exposed credentials could potentially be misused to access external services and data connected to those API keys. The incident highlights risks associated with how credentials are managed in development tools and open-source projects.
articles.whyItMatters: Exposed API keys are particularly dangerous because attackers can use them to impersonate legitimate users and access external services, potentially leading to unauthorized data access, service abuse, and further system compromise. This incident underscores the importance of secure credential management in development tools and the need for developers to rotate exposed API keys immediately.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes game, app crashes caused by recent Windows update
articles.summary: Microsoft fixed a bug in the September 2026 Windows 11 preview update that was causing games and applications to crash when using AC-3 (Dolby Digital) audio. The issue affected users who installed the KB5124010 update, but the company has now resolved the problem. This fix ensures that multimedia applications can function properly without unexpected failures.
articles.whyItMatters: Regular software updates can sometimes introduce unintended bugs that degrade system functionality and user experience. This article highlights the importance of testing updates before widespread deployment and monitoring patch quality, as even routine updates can impact critical applications and require swift remediation.
